newsitem.title: BELGIUM: ANTWERP PORT SAYS HAD RECORD FIRST HALF 1997.
newsitem.headline: ANTWERP PORT SAYS HAD RECORD FIRST HALF 1997.

text.p: The Belgian port of Antwerp said on Thursday it set three new records in the first six months of this year for container traffic, roll-on-roll-off volume and general cargo.
A total volume of 54.6 million tonnes of cargo passed through the port during the period, a rise of 4.3 percent from the first half of 1996.

Of this 27.5 million tonnes was general cargo, comprising 16 million tonnes of goods in containers, 2.6 million tonnes of ro-ro and nine million tonnes of conventional general cargo, the port authority said in a statement.
The total general cargo volume was up 7.1 percent from the first six months of last year, with container traffic up 12.1 percent and ro-ro up 12.6 percent.
Steel remained the most important component of the non-containerised general cargo sector at 4.4 million tonnes, with wood cellulose accounting for two million tonnes and fruit 1.1 million tonnes.
Car traffic rose 30.1 percent to 270,556 units.
Bulk cargo totalled 27.1 million tonnes, comprising 14.3 million tonnes of wet bulk and 12.7 million tonnes of dry bulk.
Mineral oil volume rose 11.7 percent to nine million tonnes, while ore fell 16.7 percent to 3.8 million tonnes and coal dropped 3.4 million tonnes to 2.7 million tonnes.
In the first six months of the year, 7,860 ships passed through the port, a rise of 1.3 percent on the same 1996 period, the Port Authroity said.
